title: Metric delta gating and trace-linked panel experiment log
content:
Purpose
This doc is a working log + minimal spec for an experiment to reduce noisy alerts and dashboard churn by introducing metric-delta gating tied to trace coverage, plus an associated panel slimming exercise that surfaces the trace links needed for quick investigations. The goal: only escalate when both (a) metric delta crosses a significance threshold and (b) trace+sample coverage for the affected cohort is above a minimum so operators can act.

Background and motivation
Problem: We get many small, transient metric bumps (token latency percentiles, kv-cache miss spikes, model fallback counts) that trigger alerts but lack trace coverage to investigate. These false-positives cost oncall time and increase alert fatigue. Dashboards are also overloaded — dozens of panels that rarely help when the metric signal lacks traceability.

High-level proposal
1) Metric delta gating: For a chosen set of SLI metrics (see below), compute short-window delta (current 5m vs baseline 1h or 24h depending on metric). Only mark as actionable if absolute delta and relative delta both exceed configurable thresholds.
2) Trace coverage guard: Pair metric gating with a trace-coverage check: require at least N traces (N configurable per metric) that contain anchor attributes (session_id, trace_id, model_id, route) and are sampled at the severity-weighted sample rate. If coverage < N, suppress alert to a non-urgent channel and schedule a synthetic probe.
3) Trace-linked panels: Create compact dashboard panels that are trace-first: metric sparkline + top 5 example traces (links) + quick histogram of request attributes. These panels should be small and cheap (max 1 query each) and be the default view for oncall.

Target metrics for phase 1
- serving.time_to_first_token.p50/p95 (group by route, model_variant)
- kv_cache.eviction_rate (per-tenant)
- request.fallback_rate (models falling back to lower-cost variant)
- batch.size.mean and batch.size.p95 (worker pool)
- token_cost_per_request.mean (coarse)

Gating logic (pseudocode / SQL sketch)
-- baseline_window: 1h for cache/fallback metrics, 24h for infrequent cost metrics
-- current_window: last 5 minutes

SELECT metric_name, cohort, current_val, baseline_val, delta_abs, delta_pct
FROM (
  SELECT metric_name, cohort,
         avg(value) FILTER (WHERE ts >= now() - interval '5 minutes') as current_val,
         avg(value) FILTER (WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 hour' AND ts < now() - interval '5 minutes') as baseline_val
  FROM metrics_table
  WHERE metric_name IN ('serving.time_to_first_token.p95', 'kv_cache.eviction_rate', 'request.fallback_rate')
  GROUP BY metric_name, cohort
) t
WHERE delta_abs = current_val - baseline_val
  AND delta_pct = (current_val - baseline_val) / greatest(baseline_val, 1e-6)
  AND (delta_abs > abs_thresh OR delta_pct > pct_thresh);

Then join with trace_coverage table:
SELECT t.*, tc.trace_count, tc.avg_samples_per_minute
FROM gated_metrics t
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT cohort, count(DISTINCT trace_id) as trace_count, avg(sample_rate) as avg_samples_per_minute
  FROM traces_table
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval '5 minutes' AND has_tag('investigable')
  GROUP BY cohort
) tc ON tc.cohort = t.cohort
WHERE trace_count >= min_trace_count -- configurable per metric

Trace coverage definition and annotation requirements
- A trace is counted if it contains at least one span with attributes: session_id or request_token, model_variant, route, kv_cache_key (if relevant).
- We add a lightweight tag 'investigable' when the request spans include a short context payload but not PII (see privacy notes).
- Sampling guidance: for noise-prone metrics, operate at 2–5% base sampling but scale to 20% when metric delta gating trips in the first stage (so we can collect enough examples).

Behavior on insufficient coverage
- If metric delta gating trips but trace_count < min_trace_count: 
  - Create a suppressed incident (internal, low-priority) in the incident index (no pager), post to #ops-watch with a summary and suggested synthetic probe to run.
  - Trigger an automated synthetic probe run (see linked_artifacts GH workflow) that exercises the affected route for the next 30 minutes to bootstrap trace coverage.
  - Re-evaluate every 5 minutes for 30 minutes; if coverage rises above threshold, escalate normally.

Dashboard panel design notes (trace-linked minimal panels)
- Each panel includes: small sparkline of metric (5m/1h), current vs baseline numbers, delta arrow, top 3 dimension values (tenant/route/model_variant), and 3 clickable trace links (open in trace UI with pre-filled filter). Panel must render in <400ms and cost <0.15 query units.
- Panel query pattern: pre-aggregate metric and a separate cheap trace query (trace id sample) fetched via API call, not big JOINs.
- Use a caching layer for trace links: store latest 100 trace_ids per cohort in a small Redis key for rapid surface. Redis TTL 120s.

Operator workflow (when escalation happens)
1) Oncall lands on compact panel. They see delta and 3 trace links.
2) Click trace -> opens trace UI filtered by the trace_id + session_id. The trace UI has anchors to spans: acceptor, prefetch/kvcache, model_infer, postprocess.
3) Operator annotates incident with quick tags (root-cause hypothesis: cold_kv, model_throttle, routing_fanout). That annotation is stored as a short key-value on the incident record for metric regressions.

Experiment plan and success criteria
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): feature flagging + simulation mode. Run gating logic in parallel without suppressing alerts; log decisions to a QA table. Evaluate false positive reduction and trace coverage change.
- Phase 1 (4 weeks): enable suppression for low-priority channels (#ops-watch), enable synthetic probes. Measure: alert volume down by 30% on targeted metrics, median time-to-first-valid-trace < 10 minutes after first suppressed event, operator satisfaction on quick survey >= 4/5.
- Phase 2 (6 weeks): full rollout to primary oncall channel with pagers for high-severity metrics. Evaluate incident MTTR and signal-to-noise ratio.

Risks and privacy constraints
- Traces contain customer-provided prompts / outputs; 'investigable' tag must strip or avoid payloads that are PHI/PII. Work with privacy to ensure span attributes are safe. See linked Confluence doc.
- Sampling ramp-up may temporarily increase trace query costs — cap total sampling budget (e.g., 200k trace events/day) and set budget alerts.

Open questions / TODOs
- Exact min_trace_count per metric (proposal: p95 latency -> 8 traces, kv_eviction -> 5, fallback_rate -> 10).
- Where to persist suppressed incident history for postmortem and audit (options: internal incidents DB vs. dedicated confluence log).
- UI work: small change in trace UI to accept pre-filled filter param trace_id and highlight the kv_cache span. (GH issue created: #2104)
- Ownership for synthetic probe templates (suggest: solutions-eng + SRE)

Notes from sync 2025-02-14
- Agreed: baseline window for low-signal metrics is 24h to avoid diurnal noise.
- Agreed: initial metric surface limited to 6 metrics (listed above) to keep experiment low-cost.
- Action: Maya to prototype panel wireframe (Figma link in Slack #obs-design).

Appendix: quick checklist for implementers
- [ ] Add gating SQL into metrics pipeline with feature-flag switch (FF: obs.metric_delta_gating).
- [ ] Add trace_coverage join and min_trace_count config (store in SSM or config service).
- [ ] Implement suppressed incident flow (no pager) + #ops-watch webhook.
- [ ] Implement synthetic probe job (GH workflow + runbook entry).
- [ ] Build compact trace-linked panels and Redis cache for trace links.
- [ ] Privacy review of span attributes and investigable tag.
- [ ] Dashboard cost budget monitor and alert.

End of working log: will iterate.
